plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, paying exactly that amount, ensuring non-negative profit whenever you win. Bidding below value risks losing profitable wins; bidding above value risks losing money on wins. With value $10, the optimal bid is simply $10, regardless of competitors' strategies.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: if you win, you pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid, so shading down only risks losing profitable wins, while bidding above value risks losses. With no prior rounds to inform deviation, truthful bidding of $30 maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' strategies, since you only pay what the next highest bidder bid, not your own bid. This maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying. My value is $25, so I will bid exactly $25.
